scope: Writer-side follow-up on Annex E private/second-class naming and §7.12 developer-extension declarations, focused on EC3 issues #229, #239, #340, and #732. This is not a new Annex E reader audit or proof that every writer output conforms.
primary_source: doc/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.pdf, checked with pikepdf annotation objects and the held primary layout. Physical p.893 / printed p.878 contains #229 and #340; physical p.158 / printed p.143 contains #239; physical p.157 / printed p.142 contains #732. Relevant annotation rectangles and Caret contents are recorded per issue below; pikepdf read the annotation dictionaries directly.

errata_dispositions.source_location: Annex E.2, physical p.893 / printed p.878
errata_dispositions.annotation_effect: A Caret inserts 'where otherwise stated in this specification.' into the second-class-name exception text. This narrows the exception wording; it does not add a runtime name validator. Effective §14.7.3 is an explicit specification-specific rule: PDF writers may use any names for structure types.
errata_dispositions.writer_route: The archive remediation can write supplied custom structure-role names into /RoleMap. This is a source-defined structure-type route, not Annex E developer-private data, and §14.7.3 means those names need not use a second-class prefix.

annotations.contents: where otherwise stated in this specification.

errata_dispositions.annotation_effect: The Caret/StrikeOut replacement changes ExtensionLevel numbers from 'shall' to 'should' increase monotonically over time when a developer releases multiple extensions for a BaseVersion. This is recommended chronology, not a mandatory parser check.
errata_dispositions.writer_route: No Catalog /Extensions writer currently emits developer ExtensionLevel entries.

errata_dispositions.source_location: Annex E.2 third-class names, physical p.893 / printed p.878
errata_dispositions.annotation_effect: The actual StrikeOut/Caret pair replaces the prior statement that third-class names need not be registered with the replacement: XX is reserved for private data keys, and third-class names cannot be registered in the PDF Names list. The Caret Contents states the complete replacement; the struck text is not the effective rule.
errata_dispositions.writer_route: No current generated private XX PDF key or PDF Names-list registration was found. Reader fixtures with /XX are input evidence only.

annotations.contents: XX, which has been reserved for this purpose. Any keys that are added by a developer for the purpose of adding private data to a PDF, shall begin with this prefix. Third-class names cannot be registered in the PDF Names list.

errata_dispositions.source_location: Table 49 URL row, physical p.157 / printed p.142
errata_dispositions.annotation_effect: The primary Caret/StrikeOut replaces Table 49 URL's Optional label with Required for an emitted developer extensions dictionary (StrikeOut Rect [193.850006,149.848877,405.584167,161.522003], Caret inserts Required at [401.046143,148.36235,410.122192,155.757645]); another Caret adds 'The URL assigned by the developer should be unique for each extension.' at [467.673157,136.602356,476.749207,143.99765]. The table entry is required while URL uniqueness is recommended. §7.12.6 still calls URL optional, so the effective source contains a table/subclause tension; this review does not resolve which text controls. Neither requires a reader to reject an input that omits it.
errata_dispositions.writer_route: No Catalog /Extensions or Table 49 dictionary is synthesized by current production writers. `pdf-model::requirements::Extensions::read` retains a missing URL as None for reader tolerance. Table 49's effective required label conflicts with §7.12.6's surviving 'optional URL entry' phrase; this is recorded as a source-interpretation question, not an output failure.

annotations.contents: The URL assigned by the developer should be unique for each extension.

writer_inventory.behavior: Serializes caller-provided Name bytes and generic objects; it does not select extension prefixes, construct an Extensions dictionary, or enforce Annex E name classes. This generic syntax writer is not a conformance validator.
Serializes caller-provided Assembly objects. It may emit any supplied dictionary names but does not synthesize Annex E extension declarations or enforce class/registration rules.

Update preserves existing catalog/object data and permits caller-supplied additions; its generic trailer carry-forward keeps extension-named prior entries. No automatic private PDF names or Catalog /Extensions entry are created. `an_incremental_update_repeats_a_second_class_trailer_entry` tests §7.5.6 preservation of a supplied /pdfa_NewFeature trailer entry, not Annex E name-class generation or Table 49.

Rebuild Catalogs from explicit whitelists that omit /Extensions; they do not synthesize developer-extension declarations. They copy reachable page/object dictionaries generically, so an extension-specific entry already present on a retained object may survive even when the source Catalog declaration is not in the carried whitelist. The applicable Annex E producer/retention obligation for that transformation is not resolved by a direct clause requiring preservation; this is a product-policy/traceability residual, not a confirmed conformance failure.

Edits selected Catalog entries on the existing catalog dictionary; no Annex E key or Catalog /Extensions dictionary is synthesized. Existing /Extensions is generally retained unless another explicit rewrite changes its containing object.

The archive writer can add XMP `pdfaExtension:schemas` and its XML namespace fields for described XMP properties. These are XML QNames/namespace schema records (ISO 19005/XMP), not PDF Name objects or Catalog /Extensions/Table 49 dictionaries. They are outside Annex E's #229/#239/#340/#732 rules.

A configured archive repair may add `/Chapter /Sect` or analogous supplied custom structure-type to standard-role mappings. §14.7.3 physical p.742 / printed p.727 explicitly says PDF writers may use any names for structure types. This is the explicit specification exception anticipated by #229, not an Annex E private/second-class extension-name output.

existing_assertion_quality.covers: Reader parsing of prefix-keyed Catalog Extensions and array-valued extension dictionaries, including an item with no URL.
existing_assertion_quality.does_not_cover: Writer output, registered-prefix verification, #340 private-name registration prohibition, or #732-required URL generation. The missing URL is parsed as reader tolerance.
Writer class rules or URL output.

existing_assertion_quality.covers: The newest incremental trailer restates a supplied Annex E example second-class trailer entry as required by §7.5.6.
existing_assertion_quality.does_not_cover: Selecting a legal name class for newly developed PDF extension data; Catalog /Extensions or Table 49 output.

existing_assertion_quality.assertion: crates/pdf-model/src/xmp.rs tests and crates/pdf-transform/tests/archive.rs XMP extension-schema assertions
existing_assertion_quality.covers: XMP schema-description serialization for custom metadata properties.
existing_assertion_quality.does_not_cover: PDF-level Name classes or the Catalog developer Extensions dictionary.

existing_assertion_quality.covers: Archive output can add role-map entries for source-provided custom structure type names, preserve an existing mapping, and map only an unmapped type; output is validated against its PDF/A target.
existing_assertion_quality.does_not_cover: A writer-selected developer extension name/prefix, PDF Catalog /Extensions, Table 49 BaseVersion/ExtensionLevel/URL, or private XX data. These assertions support §14.7.3's explicit any-name allowance, not Annex E class registration.

selected_adr_review.relevant_claim: Annex E.2 stays writer-side because no writer emits a developer extension.
selected_adr_review.assessment: Retain ADR 1461's writer-side classification for Annex E developer extensions/private data: no current writer synthesizes Catalog /Extensions, Table 49 entries, or private XX data. One configured archive role-map route emits supplied custom structure-type names, but §14.7.3 explicitly allows any names, the sort of specification-specific exception referenced by #229; its output assertions exist. Generic serializers can serialize caller-supplied names and update can preserve them without validating Annex E classes. Split/merge omit Catalog /Extensions while copying generic page objects; the extension-declaration/unknown-feature preservation consequence is a product-policy residual, not a confirmed Annex E violation. #340 registration and #732 URL output are not exercised. #732 also leaves a conflict: Table 49 now says required, but §7.12.6 still says optional.

test_decision: No new draft: existing archive tests cover the only identified route that emits custom PDF structure-type names, under §14.7.3's explicit allowance. No current writer constructs a PDF developer extension dictionary or private XX data; a generic serializer test would only show caller-supplied names are serialized, not Annex E conformance. Revisit if an output path starts emitting PDF-level extension data.
